task_message:
Case N11: segment the peripheral nerve sheath tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 101x101x121 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
The case is finished. Final summary:

- **Lesion:** a fusiform, T2-hyperintense peripheral nerve sheath tumor at the lateral/anterolateral aspect of the limb, spanning axial slices 63–87 (~24 mm long, ~9–10 mm thick), with a bright rim and slightly darker core (target-sign appearance) and a fine tail extending along its long axis.
- **Final mask:** v4, 1.4 mL, single connected component; extent axial 63–87, coronal 38–50, sagittal 61–70.
- **Checks performed:** the final review showed no lesion tissue past the proximal/distal, anterior/posterior or left/right ends of the mask; the outline follows the lesion border in axial, coronal and sagittal planes. A separate adjacent hyperintense tubular structure running along the bone (with an accompanying flow void, i.e. a vessel) was deliberately excluded, and the small intensity-based candidate proposals were rejected as normal adjacent tissue.
- **Confidence:** medium (departure from the lesion boundary is clean, but distinguishing the vessel-adjacent margin at the ends limits certainty).
